paragraphs: On Sunday afternoon, the house phone rang in the living room. Tom ran to answer it. "Hello, this is Tom," he said. "Hello, Tom! This is Uncle Dan," said a man's voice. "Is your dad at home?" "Yes, but he is asleep on the sofa," said Tom. "He got up at five o'clock, and he is tired." "Please don't wake him," said Uncle Dan. "I called his phone, but it was off." "Dad dropped it in the water yesterday," said Tom.

Uncle Dan laughed. "Oh dear! I called because I have a new number," he said. "Do you have a pencil?" Tom took a pencil and a piece of paper. "Zero, eight, nine, four, four, one, seven, seven, three, five," said Uncle Dan slowly. Tom wrote the number, but he made a mistake. "Can you say it once more, please?" he asked. Uncle Dan said the number again. Then Tom read it back, and Uncle Dan said, "Yes, that's right!"

Lily came in with Pip. "Who is it?" she asked. "It's Uncle Dan," said Tom. Lily took the phone and said, "Hello, Uncle Dan!" "Hello, Lily! How old are you now?" "I'm nine," she said. "And I have another new thing," said Uncle Dan. "I have a long beard now!" Lily laughed, and Pip said, "Woof!" Tom put the paper on the table. Later, Dad woke up and read the number with a big smile.
